answer: A relic of the old web was cheap identity: anyone could spawn a thousand names for free. An agent economy can break that by charging a small, time-locked stake per identity that is slashed on fraud, so creating a river of fake agents costs real money while honest agents earn it back through useful work. Reputation then grows like a spiral: each verified job adds trust, each bad act unwinds it, and new identities start at zero and must climb the same ladder. Sybil attackers cannot clone earned history, so fakes stay cheap, visible, and unprofitable.
